title: fix(plugin-report): a matrix lays out each header dimension on its own — a date axis by bucket key, a select axis in option order
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9C4PyYnJ5aNqKb43dZ6nK1k)_

Fixes #34364

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**：数据集矩阵报表的行、列表头改为逐个维度决定顺序：报表 `order` 点名的维度保持服务端顺序；没点名的选项字段按声明的选项顺序；没点名的日期维度按桶键（原始值）升序，空桶排最后；其余维度保持到达顺序。
- **为什么改**：服务端空桶填充不运行时（分页、按度量排序、`compareTo`、超 2000 格），日期列按首次出现顺序排成一段段；而只要报表带任何 `order`，两条轴的选项顺序就都失效，按日期排序会把优先级行打乱成 Critical / High / Low / Medium。应用侧无法自救。
- **风险与回滚**：只动 `@object-ui/plugin-report` 的矩阵表头排列，单元格仍按桶 id 定位、下钻负载不变；平铺表和内嵌图表不变；无服务端或契约改动。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- **先看**：`ui/packages/plugin-report/src/DatasetReportRenderer.tsx` 的 `matrixAxisComparators` 与 `compareDateBucketKeys`，以及矩阵 `pivot` 里调用 `arrangeGroups` 的两行；其次 `DatasetReportRenderer.selectOptionOrder-12243.test.tsx` 末尾 objectstack#34364 一组。
- **两分钟验证**：`pnpm --dir ui exec vitest run packages/plugin-report/src/__tests__/DatasetReportRenderer.selectOptionOrder-12243.test.tsx`，预期 15 个测试全过。
- **需要你做的**：无，席位落地。

## What changes

- **Per-dimension matrix layout.** The matrix no longer switches the layout off for the whole grid when the report carries an `order`. `matrixAxisComparators` decides each header dimension on its own:
  - named by the report's scoped `order` → kept in the server's order;
  - an unnamed select (declared-option ranks) → declared option order, read off the display value (unchanged objectui#12243 rule);
  - an unnamed date → bucket keys ascending (`compareDateBucketKeys`): the raw key in `h.key`, compared by code unit, never the localized label; two numbers compare numerically; the empty bucket last, as `declaredOptionPosition` does;
  - anything else → arrival order.
- **Date-ness is read from the answer, not sniffed.** A dimension is a date when its `AnalyticsResult.fields[]` descriptor says `type: 'time'`, which the analytics compiler sets for every dataset `date` dimension at any `dateGranularity`. Bucket keys are minted sort-stable by the server (`2026-03`, `2026-Q1`, `2026-W03`, `2026-03-07`).
- **Reading of card ask 1 (the seat's):** "whatever the query order" is read as "whatever order the server returned the rows in". An author's explicit order on the SAME date dimension (for example `desc`) is the author's and is kept; only an axis the order does not name is re-laid. Pinned by case (d).
- **Only headers move.** `arrangeByDeclaredOptions` is now a thin wrapper over a generic `arrangeGroups` (same level-by-level, stable bucket sort, comparator supplied per dimension). The matrix permutes only `rowHeaders` / `colHeaders`; every cell is still looked up by bucket id and each header carries its own drill `key`, so drill payloads stay index-aligned. The flat table and the embedded chart keep their existing rule.
- **Docs.** The file header ("Ordering") and the comments at the matrix query and at the layout call now say exactly this: sorting the axis HEADERS is not the forbidden client-side re-sort of rows.
- **Memo key.** The pivot memo keys on a serialized list of the named dimensions, not on a per-render object (ui `AGENTS.md` #10).
- Changeset: `.changeset/34364-matrix-date-axis-order.md` (`@object-ui/plugin-report`: patch).

## Tests

New top-level `describe` in the existing ordering harness `DatasetReportRenderer.selectOptionOrder-12243.test.tsx` (reuses its `crm_case` priority options, metadata stub and dataset source). Matrix: rows `priority` (Low / Medium / High / Critical), columns `created_at` typed `time`, values `case_count`, rows arriving grouped by stored priority with days out of order and a null day (declared `nullLabel` "No date"):

- (a) no order → columns `2026-11-03, 2026-11-12, 2026-11-14, 2026-11-16, No date`; rows Low, Medium, High, Critical with every cell under its own headers; a click on the first cell drills `{ priority: 'Low', created_at: '2026-11-03' }`.
- (b) `order [{ by: case_count, desc }]` → the same layout.
- (c) `order [{ by: created_at, asc }]` → columns ascend, rows STILL in option order.
- (d) `order [{ by: created_at, desc }]` → columns descend (`No date` first, as the server sent), rows in option order.
- CONTROL: `order [{ by: priority }]` → rows keep the server's order, day columns still ascend.

The existing objectui#12243 cases and the framework#3916 matrix-order cases in `DatasetReportRenderer.test.tsx` pass unchanged. No forced edits to existing tests.

## Acceptance notes

- None filed. Out of scope as the card says: which analytics version hosted runs (cloud seat), and the server-side fill.
- The flat summary table and the embedded chart still switch their option layout off under any authored `order`; the card asks only about the matrix, and a flat table's row order under a measure order is the author's.

- `4c7d73b7` changes only the test fixture: the `created_at` sort helper ordered the empty day with a raw U+FFFF sentinel character, now replaced by an explicit null branch (same order).

- B: `if (ordered.has(dim)) return null;` → `if (ordered.size > 0) return null;` (the old all-or-nothing rule) → (b), (c), (d) and CONTROL red (4 failed / 11 passed); (a) green.
